THE SEED IDEA (from a Telegram brainstorm between the user, Alexander Didenko, and a friend — original Russian, translated):

- "Морской бой, в котором ты имеешь право переставлять корабли как угодно, если данные, которые ты сообщил при выстрелах врага остаются верными (попал, убил, мимо). И ты можешь это делать перед каждым выстрелом врага."
  => Battleship where the DEFENDER may rearrange their fleet arbitrarily between enemy shots, as long as every answer already given (hit / kill / miss) remains true of the new arrangement. Allowed before every enemy shot.
- "Понятно, что машина это легко сделает. Но вот человеку такая комбинаторика может быть сложна."
  => A machine can do this combinatorics trivially; a human cannot. (=> the game must do the combinatorics FOR the human player, and make it legible.)
- "это тоже будет восьмибитная игра" => it must be an 8-bit game.
- "тут идея в множественности реальностей" => the theme is multiplicity of realities.
- "у тебя есть двигатель Алькубьерре. Он не позволяет уйти ни в будущее ни в прошлое, но он позволяет по бране перейти в соседнюю версию реальности где космические корабли по другому стояли."
  => An Alcubierre drive: no time travel, but you can cross the BRANE into a neighbouring version of reality where the ships stood differently. (This is the in-fiction justification for rearranging.)
- "Лавкрафтовскую историю надо брать. Непознанный темный бог искажает реальность там, где ты ее не пришпилил."
  => Lovecraftian framing: an unknowable dark god twists reality wherever you have NOT pinned it down. (This is the perfect fictional statement of the core mechanic: unobserved = unfixed = hostile.)
- "Либо это битва с доктором Стрэнжем, который смотрит 14млн вариантов сценариев и выбирает нужный" (+ a Doctor Strange gif)
  => The 14,000,605 futures reference. Suggests a visible COUNTER of remaining consistent realities.
- "Смотри, каждая твоя перестановка открывает дорогу в мультивселенную" / "Но каждый мой выстрел накрывает корабли сразу во всех ветках!"
  => Every rearrangement opens a road into the multiverse; a shot lands in ALL branches at once.
- "есть особый снаряд которым я могу накрыть сразу несколько альтернативных веток"
  => a special munition that covers several alternative branches at once.
- Warhammer 40k GELLER FIELD was raised: "Генераторы поля создают вокруг корабля почти невидимую энергетическую завесу — своеобразный пузырь реальности. Внутри этого пузыря продолжают действовать законы физического пространства-времени, а не хаотичные и извращённые правила Имматериума."
  => A bubble of STABLE reality. Obvious mechanic: project it onto a region and reality inside is PINNED — cannot shift any more. Literally "пришпилить реальность".
- Working title floated by the friend: "Рыцари и лжецы в мультивселенной безумия" (Knights and Liars in the Multiverse of Madness).
- The user's verdict on the state of the idea: "короче надо докрутить" (needs finishing/tightening).

WHAT THE USER ASKED FOR NOW (verbatim):
"Мне нужна новая 8битная игра. Я вообще без понятия как ты ее сделаешь и в каком лоре. Но она должна быть такая же крутая как десант Nostromo."
=> A new 8-bit game, lore is my call, it must be as cool as the Nostromo landing game (the existing project 'nostromo-gambit'). The user then said: work maximally autonomously, they are going to sleep. So: NO questions can be asked. Make confident decisions and justify them.

MY WORKING DIRECTION (challenge it if it is wrong, but this is the frame):
The player is the ATTACKER hunting a fleet that exists in superposition. The enemy fleet is not "hidden" — it is genuinely UNDETERMINED, collapsing only where the player has pinned it. The HUD's centrepiece is a big counter of remaining consistent realities, ticking down from millions. The visual signature is GHOST FLEETS: faint flickering silhouettes of sampled possible placements drawn over the enemy grid, converging into solid hulls as the possibility space collapses. Symmetrically, the PLAYER's own fleet also evades — the machine does that combinatorics for the human — but evading costs a resource and feeds the dark god.

CONSTRAINT: the deliverable must be a finished, polished, self-contained 8-bit game of the same production quality and scale as the existing 'nostromo-gambit' project. Not a prototype, not a toy. It must be genuinely fun to a human, not just conceptually clever.



=== REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF (nostromo-gambit — the quality bar) ===
Path: G:\Другие компьютеры\PAULEKMAN\dev\nostromo-gambit  — this is a MIRROR (source-only, no node_modules). The LIVE, runnable working copy is C:\dev\nostromo-gambit. They are byte-identical except (a) C: has one extra file scripts\mutation-check.mjs, (b) C:\dev\...\public\app.js is 3 lines newer (a banner-phase reset). Sync direction is C: -> G: via `npm run mirror` (scripts/mirror-to-drive.mjs). NEVER run npm install on G:.
Stack: NO BUILD TOOLING AT ALL. No bundler, no transpiler, no framework, no CSS preprocessor, no TypeScript, no test framework package.

- Runtime: Node >= 22, `"type": "module"`, plain ESM `.mjs` everywhere on the server.
- Exactly ONE npm dependency in the whole project: `"chess.js": "1.4.0"`. Zero devDependencies. Tests run on the built-in `node --test`.
- Server: raw `node:http` + a hand-written 9-route router (src/server/http.mjs), a hand-written static file server (src/server/static.mjs) and a hand-written SSE hub (src/server/sse.mjs). Comment at the top of http.mjs: "Маршрутизатор на node:http. Никаких фреймворков — маршрутов девять."
- Client: three plain ES modules loaded with `<script type="module" src="/app.js">`, no imports from any CDN, no npm packages on the front end. `public/app.js` uses top-level `await` (it is a module).
- Rendering: NOT canvas. NOT React. Plain DOM + CSS transforms + inline SVG generated in JS. Board = 64 permanent `<div class="sq">` in a CSS grid + a separate absolutely-positioned `.pieces` layer where each piece is a `<div class="piece">` moved by `transform: translate(%,%)`.
- Transport: one GET /api/state + one SSE stream GET /api/events + five POST endpoints. No WebSocket.
- External engine: official Stockfish binary, downloaded at setup time into %LOCALAPPDATA%, driven as a SEPARATE PROCESS over UCI (deliberate weak coupling for GPL reasons). Not bundled, not in the repo.
- Zero external assets: no image files, no font files, no audio files, no icon files. The favicon is an inline `data:image/svg+xml` in index.html.
- package.json scripts: setup / start / test / test:unit / test:real / selfplay / audit / e2e / mirror / bench.
- .npmrc pins the npm cache to C: (`cache=C:\Users\user\AppData\Local\npm-cache`, `fund=false`, `audit=false`).
Scale: ~6149 lines of game code.
Files: Runtime game code = 6,149 lines (src 4,215 + public 1,934). Shipped total including tests and tooling = 8,857 lines of code + 350 lines of Russian docs.

public/ — 1,934 lines, THE PART THE NEW GAME MOST NEEDS TO MATCH
  theme.css        571 lines / 18.3 KB  — the entire 8-bit CRT look
  app.js           547 lines / 22.2 KB  — event stream, rendering, input, start screen
  sprites.js       410 lines / 11.4 KB  — 16x16 ASCII bitmaps -> SVG
  board.js         226 lines /  9.4 KB  — 64 squares, piece diffing, pointer input
  index.html       180 lines /  8.7 KB  — full static skeleton, every panel pre-declared

src/ — 4,215 lines
  game/dropGenerator.mjs 474  game/fen.mjs 282  game/dropRules.mjs 251
  game/marginal.mjs 222  game/game.mjs 356  game/packages.mjs 166
  game/sharpness.mjs 121  game/storytellers.mjs 107  game/computer.mjs 76
  game/rng.mjs 76  game/dice.mjs 51  game/fischer.mjs 60
  engine/uci.mjs 407  engine/pool.mjs 277  engine/evaluate.mjs 166
  engine/registry.mjs 145  engine/mock.mjs 141  engine/analysis.mjs 123
  server/main.mjs 360  server/http.mjs 115  server/sse.mjs 114  server/static.mjs 56
  shared/paths.mjs 69

scripts/ — 1,053 lines
  get-stockfish.mjs 471, selfplay.mjs 305, bench-drops.mjs 139, corpus.mjs 66,
  mirror-to-drive.mjs 60, stockfish.lock.json 12  (+ mutation-check.mjs on C: only)

test/ — 1,655 lines, 118 tests, all green in ~14 s
  unit/*.test.mjs (7 files, 101 tests) run against an in-process MockEngine so they
  finish in seconds; integration/http.test.mjs (229 lines, 17 tests) boots the REAL
  server on port 0 and parses raw SSE frames; helpers/server.mjs 112;
  fixtures/fake-engine.mjs 156; e2e/serve-for-e2e.mjs 35.

Docs: README.md 169 lines, REPORT.md 181 lines — both in Russian, both written as prose
for the user (not for a machine), both include a "known limitations / what was NOT done"
section. Matching that documentation standard is part of the quality bar.
Aesthetic: "Ship's terminal": green phosphor vs amber phosphor on near-black, scanlines, vignette, brightness flicker. Every pixel is CSS or generated SVG — comment at the top of theme.css: "Всё рисуется CSS — ни одной картинки, ни одного внешнего шрифта."

PALETTE (public/theme.css :root, exact hex):
  --phosphor:       #7dff9b   green phosphor = side 1 (marines / white)
  --phosphor-dim:   #3d8a52   secondary text, borders on buttons
  --phosphor-faint: #1c3d27   tertiary text, coordinates, "nothing here yet"
  --amber:          #ffb347   amber phosphor = side 2 (xenos / black), all warnings
  --amber-dim:      #8a5f26
  --alert:          #ff4d4d   only for the broken-link dot
  --bg:             #050a06   page ground
  --panel:          #0a140c   panel fill
  --panel-edge:     #16301c   every 1px border, every separator
  --light-square:   #17301d
  --dark-square:    #0d1e11
Literal one-off colors: check square background #3a0f0f; eval-bar label text #dfffe8 on
rgba(5,10,6,0.78); overlay scrim rgba(5,10,6,0.9); glow shadows are
rgba(125,255,155,0.x) for green and rgba(255,179,71,0.x) for amber.

SPRITE PALETTE (public/sprites.js, per side, 4 colors each):
  w: { x:'#06170c'  outline, '#':'#7dff9b' body, o:'#dcffe6' highlight, '*':'#ffd166' accent }
  b: { x:'#1d0f00'  outline, '#':'#ffb347' body, o:'#ffe3ba' highlight, '*':'#b6ff5a' accent }
Doctrine stated in the file: the two sides differ by HUE, not by brightness, so they stay
legible on a dim CRT — and both hues are real period monitor phosphors.

FONT: `--font: 'Consolas', 'DejaVu Sans Mono', 'Courier New', monospace;` — system mono
only, no webfont, no @font-face, nothing loaded from Google Fonts. Body 14px,
`letter-spacing: 0.04em`. Titles are wide-tracked uppercase: `.title` 17px/0.22em,
`.start-title` 25px/0.3em, panel `<h2>` 11px/0.2em, buttons 12px/0.12em.
Text-shadow glow on titles only: `0 0 8px rgba(125,255,155,0.5)` / `0 0 14px …0.45`.

SPRITE TECHNIQUE (this is the signature move, copy it verbatim):
16 rows x 16 chars of ASCII, one string per row, 4 symbols: `.` transparent, `x` outline,
`#` body, `o` highlight, `*` accent. `spriteSvg()` walks each row, run-length-merges
horizontally identical pixels into one `<rect>`, and emits
`<svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" shape-rendering="crispEdges" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet">`.
Results are memoized in a `Map` keyed `set:color:type`. The RLE is not decoration — the
comment says without it the board would cost >4000 DOM nodes in pieces alone.
Two full sets exist: `classic` (traditional silhouettes) and `xeno` (marines vs xenomorphs),
switchable at runtime from the settings drawer.

RESOLUTION / SCALING: there is no fixed canvas. Board is `--board-max: min(72vh, 560px)`
(mobile: `min(92vw, 520px)`), squares are a `repeat(8,1fr)` grid, each piece is
`width:12.5%; height:12.5%` with `.piece svg { padding: 7%; image-rendering: pixelated }`.
So a 16x16 bitmap renders at ~65px and stays crisp via crispEdges + pixelated.

CRT EFFECT — one pseudo-element over everything, click-through:
  body::after { position:fixed; inset:0; pointer-events:none; z-index:100;
    background:
      repeating-linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(0,0,0,.22) 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px),
      radial-gradient(ellipse at center, transparent 55%, rgba(0,0,0,.55) 100%);
    animation: flicker 5.5s infinite steps(60); }
`steps(60)` is what makes the flicker read as a CRT and not as a fade. The flicker
keyframes only dip at 97%/99% (0.93 / 0.96) — subtle, never distracting.

MOTION VOCABULARY (exact durations — reuse these numbers, they are tuned):
  piece move          transform 180ms ease-out (piece never re-created, only translated)
  drop landing        340ms cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1), starts 44px above with
                      scale(1.7) and opacity 0 — overshoot reads as a LANDING
  shockwave ring      460ms ease-out, scale(0.2)->2.2, opacity .7->0, amber border
  banner slide        translateY(-100%) -> 0, 220ms ease-out
  drawer slide        translateX(100%) -> 0, 200ms ease-out
  eval bar            height/width 260ms ease-out
  toast               opacity+translateY 200ms, auto-hides after 3400ms
  die shake           90ms infinite ±1px/±4deg; spin redraws every 70ms for 700ms
  boot typewriter     9ms per character, 120ms per line break
`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` appears THREE times and kills the flicker, the
piece transition, the landing animation and the shockwave. Non-negotiable for parity.

LAYOUT: one CSS grid with named areas —
  grid-template-areas: 'head head head' / 'evalbar board side' / 'foot foot foot'
  grid-template-columns: 42px var(--board-max) minmax(300px, 1fr)
  max-width 1240px, `overflow:hidden` on html/body (desktop), gap 12px, padding 10px 14px.
At `max-width: 980px` it collapses to a single column, areas reorder to
'head' 'evalbar' 'board' 'foot' 'side', and the vertical eval bar becomes a horizontal
22px strip whose gradient direction flips. Note the file ends with a DUPLICATED narrow
media block and an explicit comment explaining that a later `.foot { flex-wrap: nowrap }`
rule won on equal specificity, so the mobile rules had to be repeated last. That kind of
comment — the fix plus why — is the house style.

CHROME DETAILS worth copying: 1px `--panel-edge` borders on everything; panel headers are
11px 0.2em uppercase dim-green on a bordered strip; buttons are transparent with a dim
border and hover = 10% tint + 8px glow; segmented controls (`.seg`) collapse borders with
`border-right-width:0` except `:last-child`, and the active one gets
`inset 0 0 10px rgba(125,255,155,.18)`; dice are 3x3 CSS grids of 5px round `<i>` pips;
`.pips` uses `●●●○○` text characters for remaining rolls; separators in the move log are
`border-top: 1px dashed var(--amber-dim)` with the text `═══ ДЕСАНТ #3 ═══`.
Audio: THERE IS NO AUDIO. NONE. I grepped the entire project (both the G: mirror and the C: live copy) for AudioContext / createOscillator / webkitAudioContext / `new Audio(` / sound / звук / audio — zero matches. There is no audio engine, no chiptune player, no sound file, no mute toggle, no volume setting, no `<audio>` element, no gesture-unlock code.

This is the single biggest gap in the reference project and the clearest place where the second game can EXCEED the bar rather than merely match it. Do not go looking for a helper to copy — there is nothing. If the new game wants sound, it must be written from scratch.

Constraints the new audio code must respect to stay consistent with the project's doctrine:
1. Zero external assets and zero dependencies. That rules out sample files and audio libraries; it means WebAudio synthesis (oscillators + gain envelopes + a noise buffer) written by hand, the same way sprites are hand-generated rather than shipped as PNGs.
2. Autoplay policy: nostromo-gambit has an explicit first-click gate already available — the `#start-go` "▶ НАЧАТЬ ОПЕРАЦИЮ" button on the start screen is guaranteed to be a user gesture. That is where `new AudioContext()` should be created / resumed.
3. It must honour the same accessibility instinct as `prefers-reduced-motion`: an audio on/off checkbox belongs in the settings drawer next to "Показывать шкалу оценки", persisted through the same settings POST, and it must default in a way that never surprises.
4. Every sound needs a named, motivated trigger the same way every animation does — the existing event vocabulary gives the hook points for free: `move`, `drop:start`, `drop:progress`, `drop:done`, `drop:skipped`, `dice`, `thinking`, check, game over, boot typewriter keyclick.
5. Palette discipline translates to audio: two timbres for the two sides (green/amber), one alert timbre, nothing else — the same "two hues, not two brightnesses" logic.
Architecture: SHAPE: a local single-player-at-one-screen web app with an authoritative Node server. The client is deliberately stupid. Top of public/app.js, verbatim:

  // Клиент намеренно ничего не решает сам: легальность ходов, расписание десанта
  // и счёт жетонов живут на сервере и приходят готовыми. Здесь только три вещи —
  // отрисовка, ввод указателя и тайминги анимаций.

THERE IS NO GAME LOOP. No requestAnimationFrame, no setInterval tick, no fixed timestep,
no update()/draw() split anywhere in the project. The app is 100% event-driven: server
state changes -> SSE frame -> `applyState(next)` -> full re-render of a small DOM. All
motion is delegated to CSS transitions/animations. The only timers in the client are the
dice spin (`setInterval(…, 70)` for 700 ms), the boot typewriter (chained `setTimeout`),
the toast dismissal (3400 ms) and shockwave cleanup (500 ms). If the second game needs a
real-time loop, that pattern must be invented — there is nothing here to copy.

SERVER STATE MACHINE — `class Game` (src/game/game.mjs), 356 lines:
  phase: 'idle' | 'dropping' | 'over'   (set in #refreshGameOver)
  version: monotonically incremented on EVERY mutation; it is both the SSE event id and
           the optimistic-concurrency token.
  Own journal instead of the library's: `atoms[]` (each `{kind:'move'|'drop', …}`) plus a
  parallel `snapshots[]` stack of FENs. Reason is documented at the top of the file —
  chess.js 1.4.0 `load()` calls `clear()` and destroys its own history, and the drop
  mechanic must rebuild the position from FEN, so undo/move-list/threefold would have
  silently vanished. There is a regression test for exactly this.
  Stable piece identity: `this.pieces` is a Map square -> `{id:'p17', type, color}`.
  IDs are assigned from a module-level `nextPieceId` counter and are what makes the client
  animate instead of blink. `#applyPieceMove(m)` transfers the id using the SEMANTICS of
  the move (en-passant victim square, castling rook hop, promotion type swap) because you
  cannot infer identity by diffing two positions.
  Honest degradation: after undo, ids are re-issued (`#rebuildPieceIds`) and the board
  redraws wholesale, with a comment saying this is more honest than pretending.

APP ORCHESTRATOR — `class App` (src/server/main.mjs), 360 lines: owns sessionId (randomUUID),
Game, SseHub, EnginePool, AnalysisEngine, Rng, and the `dropInProgress` / `dropAbort` pair.
Async work (computer move, drop search) is deliberately NOT awaited inside the HTTP handler:

  // Намеренно не await: ход считается в фоне, а состояние уезжает клиенту событием.
  // Иначе HTTP-ответ на ход человека ждал бы, пока движок додумает свой…

and every background task re-checks `this.game.version !== versionAtStart` before applying
its result, because the game may have been reset/undone while it was thinking.

SCREENS (there are no routes; screens are stacked z-indexed overlays in one HTML file):
  .start   z-index 90  full-screen start card, `.off` hides it
  .drawer  z-index 60  settings, slides in from the right
  .overlay z-index 50  two of them: game-over card and promotion picker; `.on` shows
  .toast   z-index 70  transient message
  body::after z-index 100 CRT layer above everything, pointer-events none
The start screen is shown ONLY when there is nothing to resume — last 8 lines of app.js:
`const gameInProgress = state && (state.moveLog.length > 0 || state.dropLog.length > 0)`;
if resuming it shows the toast «ПАРТИЯ ВОССТАНОВЛЕНА» instead. This exists because a
reload mid-game used to cover a live board with a screen whose only button would erase it.

HTTP API (src/server/http.mjs): GET /api/state, GET /api/events, GET /health,
POST /api/move | /api/roll | /api/new-game | /api/undo | /api/settings,
POST /api/_test/fen (only when NODE_ENV=test). One `STATUS` table maps error codes to
HTTP statuses (409 for conflicts, 422 for illegal move, 503 for engine down). Body limit
64 KB. Errors are caught so a bad request never kills a game in progress.

OPTIMISTIC CONCURRENCY: client sends `version: state.version` with move/roll/undo; a
mismatch returns `{code:'STALE_VERSION'}` and the client treats it as non-error and just
re-reads state (`if (data.code === 'STALE_VERSION') { await refresh(); return data; }`).

EVENT STREAM: exactly ONE multiplexed SSE endpoint, with the reason spelled out — HTTP/1.1
allows ~6 connections per origin, two streams x two tabs already eats four. Event names:
`snapshot`, `state`, `move`, `settings` (all carry a full snapshot and an `id:`),
plus volatile `eval`, `thinking`, `drop:progress` (NO `id:`, so they cannot poison
Last-Event-ID), plus `dice`, `drop:start`, `drop:done`, `drop:skipped`.
A 200-frame ring buffer replays from Last-Event-ID; if there is a gap it falls back to a
full snapshot. 15 s heartbeat comments, `retry: 3000`, `setNoDelay(true)` (Nagle was
batching 60-byte eval frames into 40 ms jerks), `X-Accel-Buffering: no`, `no-transform`.

INPUT (public/board.js `#bindPointer`): Pointer Events only — NOT HTML5 drag&drop, with
the reason in a comment (ghost image, no touch support, no control over animation). Two
interaction modes on the same handler: drag (pointerdown -> capture -> pointermove sets
`transform` in px -> pointerup hit-tests) and click-click (select source, then click a
highlighted target). `#squareFromPoint(x,y)` converts client coords via
`getBoundingClientRect()` and a /8 floor. On release the piece is ALWAYS snapped back
locally and the server's echo is what actually moves it. `board.setLocked()` freezes input
during a drop and after game over. `.board { touch-action: none; user-select: none }`.
Keyboard: only `Escape` (closes drawer + promo, clears selection).

PERSISTENCE: there is none on the client — no localStorage, no cookies, no save file.
State lives in server memory; a page reload re-fetches it. Runtime artifacts (engine
binary, selfplay NDJSON, PID registry) live in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\nostromo-gambit\` via
src/shared/paths.mjs, deliberately NOT next to the sources, because the source folder is
on a Google Drive virtual volume. `writeJsonAtomic()` = write .tmp then rename.

DETERMINISM: `makeRng(seed)` (xorshift128+) everywhere; `Math.random` appears exactly once
in the whole client and only to spin the dice faces visually. Same seed reproduces the
whole game including the Fischer start position (`fischerFen(makeRng('fischer:'+seed))`).
Reusable helpers: Verbatim signatures of the helpers worth lifting into the second game.

PIXEL-ART RENDERER (public/sprites.js) — the highest-value single function:
  export const PALETTES = { w: {...}, b: {...} }          // 4 keys: x # o *
  export function spriteSvg(setName, color, type) -> string   // memoized, RLE'd SVG
  export const PIECE_LETTER = { p:'П', n:'К', b:'С', r:'Л', q:'Ф', k:'Кр' }
  export const PIECE_NAME   = { p:'пешка', ... }
Generalize by renaming `setName/color/type` to `(setName, paletteKey, spriteKey)` and
keeping the ASCII-bitmap-as-string-array authoring format unchanged.

BOARD / SPRITE LAYER (public/board.js) — a reusable "grid of cells + diffed sprite layer":
  export function squareName(file, rank)
  export class BoardView {
    constructor({ squaresEl, piecesEl, boardEl, onSelect })
    render(board, { legalMoves = {}, lastMove = null, checkSquare = null,
                    reinforced = [], landedIds = null } = {})
    select(sq); clearSelection();
    shockwave(squares);                  // spawns .shock spans, self-removing after 500ms
    setLocked(locked); setPieceSet(name, badges);
    #buildSquares(); #bindPointer(); #squareFromPoint(x, y); #placePiece(el, square);
    #createPiece(p);
  }
The load-bearing idea to copy: cells are built ONCE and never re-created; entities live in
a sibling absolutely-positioned layer, are keyed by a server-assigned stable id, and are
moved with `--tx/--ty` custom properties + `transform: translate(var(--tx), var(--ty))`.
That one decision is what turns "re-render" into "animation".

TOAST (public/app.js) — 6 lines, uses a property on the function itself as the timer slot:
  function toast(text) { el.toast.textContent = text; el.toast.classList.add('on');
    clearTimeout(toast.t); toast.t = setTimeout(() => el.toast.classList.remove('on'), 3400); }

TYPEWRITER BOOT SEQUENCE (public/app.js):

HONESTY AS A DESIGN PRINCIPLE. This is the strongest through-line and the thing that makes
the project feel expensive. When something cannot be done properly it is disabled and said
out loud, in the UI, not hidden: Fischer castling is off and the start screen says so;
a failed drop refunds the die and prints the reason; a widened tolerance is written into
the drop log as «ДОПУСК РАСШИРЕН ДО ±45 СП»; undo after a drop admits it must redraw the
whole board. README and REPORT both end with «Известные ограничения» / «Что осталось
несделанным». The second game must have that section too.

OPENING. Not a splash screen — a configuration terminal, exactly like an era game. The
boot text types itself character by character (9 ms/char, 120 ms/line) above the title,
then a single card asks EVERYTHING at once via segmented buttons: player 1 human/computer,
player 2 human/computer, computer level 1–5, planner, start position, dice rolls per
player, auto-drop frequency. Every option has a live one-line explanatory note under it
(`.opt-note`, amber-dim) that changes as you select — the level note, the planner blurb,
the Fischer caveat. One amber call-to-action: «▶ НАЧАТЬ ОПЕРАЦИЮ». Under it, one honest
line about the 32-piece ceiling.

DIFFICULTY. Five named levels with character, not numbers: 1 РЯДОВОЙ / 2 КАПРАЛ /
3 СЕРЖАНТ / 4 ЛЕЙТЕНАНТ / 5 MU-TH-UR 6000 («Полная сила на этой машине. Удачи.»).
Default is 3. Crucially, weakening is done by MultiPV move selection within a `slackCp`
window (220/130/60/20/0), NOT by cutting depth — with the stated reason: a depth-starved
engine plays *stranger*, not weaker; it still never blunders two-move tactics but stops
having a plan. Even level 1 is forbidden from gifting a queen.

PACING. Turn-based, no timers, no pressure. The drama is manufactured in two places:
(1) the drop — a banner slides down over the board, the board dims to 0.55 and goes
`cursor:wait`, a phase-weighted progress bar advances through four named phases
(weights 0.05/0.2/0.55/1.0 so the bar never lies about which stage it is in), and it ends
with pieces falling from above with an overshoot plus amber shockwave rings and a toast;
(2) the dice — 700 ms of shaking, faces reshuffling every 70 ms, then the readout line
that tells you exactly what you bought. Search takes 4–6 s in practice and REPORT.md says
plainly that this was over the 2.5 s target — the progress bar with meaningful phase names
is the accepted mitigation: "ожидание читается как работа, а не как зависание."

WHAT MAKES IT FEEL GOOD. (a) Nothing ever blinks: stable piece ids mean every change is a
motion. (b) Every number shown is explained somewhere — the drop log prints
`+0.34 → +0.29 · Δ -5 сп · ЦЕЛЬ 0 · 4.2 с` and the header prints the hold count.
(c) Personality lives in tables, not in code branches — three "planners" (МАТЬ / БИШОП /
ЭШ, borrowed conceptually from RimWorld storytellers) differ only by weights and tolerance,
each with a `tone: { start, done, skipped }` string triple; ЭШ's line is
«ВЫСАДКА ВЫПОЛНЕНА. НЕ МОГУ ЛГАТЬ О ВАШИХ ШАНСАХ.». (d) Tension is built into the dice
math rather than into UI noise: sum buys tonnage, spread buys bias, and a double gives max
tonnage with ZERO bias while 6–1 gives max bias with almost no tonnage — you cannot have
both. (e) The one aesthetic ruling the user made mid-build is recorded in REPORT.md and
worth internalizing: the eval bar used to be "green vs empty", which speaks the language of
white and black; it was recolored to green-vs-amber so it speaks the language of THIS
game's two sides.

ENDING. A centered card over a 0.9 scrim: the reason in huge tracked caps («МАТ»), one
statistics line («Ходов: 47 · Десантов: 6 · Фигур на доске: 21»), and two buttons —
«НОВАЯ ПАРТИЯ» (returns to the configuration terminal, never straight into a game) and
«ПОСМОТРЕТЬ ПАРТИЮ» (dismisses the card so you can study the final position). There is also
`Game.toPgn()` which exports the game with drops as PGN comments, so a game can be re-read.

//   .  прозрачно      x  контур       #  тело
//   o  блик           *  акцент (визор морпеха, кислота ксеноморфа)

export const PALETTES = {
  w: { x: '#06170c', '#': '#7dff9b', o: '#dcffe6', '*': '#ffd166' },
  b: { x: '#1d0f00', '#': '#ffb347', o: '#ffe3ba', '*': '#b6ff5a' },
};

const cache = new Map();

/**
 * Разворачивает битмап в SVG. Соседние пиксели одного цвета склеиваются в один
 * прямоугольник по горизонтали: без этого на доску уходило бы больше четырёх тысяч
 * узлов DOM только под фигуры.
 */
export function spriteSvg(setName, color, type) {
  const key = `${setName}:${color}:${type}`;
  if (cache.has(key)) return cache.get(key);

  const set = SETS[setName] || SETS.xeno;
  const rows = (set[color] || set.w)[type] || CLASSIC[type];
  const palette = PALETTES[color];
  const parts = [];

  for (let y = 0; y < rows.length; y++) {
    const row = rows[y];
    let x = 0;
    while (x < row.length) {
      const ch = row[x];
      if (ch === '.' || ch === ' ') { x += 1; continue; }
      let run = 1;
      while (x + run < row.length && row[x + run] === ch) run += 1;
      const fill = palette[ch] || palette['#'];
      parts.push(`<rect x="${x}" y="${y}" width="${run}" height="1" fill="${fill}"/>`);
      x += run;
    }

  /**
   * Указатель, а не нативный drag&drop: последний тащит призрачную картинку,
   * не работает на касании и не даёт управлять анимацией. Плюс поддержан
   * режим «клик по источнику — клик по цели», которым играет большинство.
   */
  #bindPointer() {
    let dragging = null;

    this.boardEl.addEventListener('pointerdown', (ev) => {
      if (this.locked) return;
      const sq = this.#squareFromPoint(ev.clientX, ev.clientY);
      if (!sq) return;

      // Второй клик по подсвеченной цели завершает ход.
      if (this.selected && this.legalMoves[this.selected]?.includes(sq)) {
        this.onSelect({ from: this.selected, to: sq });
        this.clearSelection();
        return;
      }

      const piece = this.board.find((p) => p.square === sq);
      if (!piece || !this.legalMoves[sq]) { this.clearSelection(); return; }

      this.select(sq);
      const el = this.pieceEls.get(piece.id);
      if (!el) return;
      dragging = { from: sq, el, pointerId: ev.pointerId, moved: false };
      el.classList.add('dragging');
      this.boardEl.setPointerCapture(ev.pointerId);
      ev.preventDefault();
    });

    this.boardEl.addEventListener('pointermove', (ev) => {
      if (!dragging) return;
      const rect = this.boardEl.getBoundingClientRect();
      const size = rect.width / 8;
      const x = ev.clientX - rect.left - size / 2;
      const y = ev.clientY - rect.top - size / 2;
      dragging.moved = true;
      dragging.el.style.transform = `translate(${x}px, ${y}px)`;
    });

    const finish = (ev) => {
      if (!dragging) return;
      const { from, el, moved } = dragging;
      dragging = null;
      el.classList.remove('dragging');
      el.style.transform = '';
      this.#placePiece(el, from); // вернём на место; сервер подтвердит настоящий ход
      try { this.boardEl.releasePointerCapture(ev.pointerId); } catch { /* захват мог уже отпуститься сам */ }
      if (!moved) return; // это был обычный клик — выбор уже сделан
      const to = this.#squareFromPoint(ev.clientX, ev.clientY);
      if (!to || to === from) return;
      if (!this.legalMoves[from]?.includes(to)) return;
      this.onSelect({ from, to });
      this.clearSelection();
    };

    this.boardEl.addEventListener('pointerup', finish);
    this.boardEl.addEventListener('pointercancel', finish);
  }

  #squareFromPoint(x, y) {
    const rect = this.boardEl.getBoundingClientRect();
    const f = Math.floor(((x - rect.left) / rect.width) * 8);
    const r = 8 - Math.floor(((y - rect.top) / rect.height) * 8);
    if (f < 0 || f > 7 || r < 1 || r > 8) return null;
    return squareName(f, r);
  }

export class Rng {
  constructor(seed = 'nostromo') {
    this.seed = String(seed);
    const [a, b, c, d] = hashSeed(seed);
    this.s = new Uint32Array([a, b, c, d]);
    // Прокручиваем, чтобы близкие сиды не давали похожих первых чисел.
    for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) this.next();
  }
  next() {                                   // xorshift128+, uint32
    let t = this.s[3]; const s0 = this.s[0];
    this.s[3] = this.s[2]; this.s[2] = this.s[1]; this.s[1] = s0;
    t ^= t << 11; t ^= t >>> 8;
    this.s[0] = (t ^ s0 ^ (s0 >>> 19)) >>> 0;
    return this.s[0];
  }
  float() { return this.next() / 4294967296; }
  int(min, max) { if (max < min) return min; return min + (this.next() % (max - min + 1)); }
  pick(arr) { if (!arr || arr.length === 0) return undefined; return arr[this.next() % arr.length]; }
  shuffle(arr) { for (let i = arr.length - 1; i > 0; i--) { const j = this.next() % (i + 1); [arr[i], arr[j]] = [arr[j], arr[i]]; } return arr; }
  weighted(items, weightOf = (x) => x.weight) {
    const total = items.reduce((s, x) => s + Math.max(0, weightOf(x)), 0);
    if (total <= 0) return this.pick(items);
    let roll = this.float() * total;
    for (const item of items) { roll -= Math.max(0, weightOf(item)); if (roll <= 0) return item; }
    return items[items.length - 1];
  }
  /** Отдельный поток случайности, привязанный к метке — чтобы ветки не сдвигали друг друга. */
  fork(label) { return new Rng(`${this.seed}:${label}:${this.next()}`); }
}
export function makeRng(seed) { return new Rng(seed); }

Approach: ## The headline result: on the right board, you don't need a sampler at all

I measured this rather than guessed it. **The entire possibility space of an 8×8 board with fleet [4,3,3,2] under the no-touch rule is 3,562,232 configurations, and it fits in 13.6 MB and builds in 68 ms.**

That single fact collapses the whole "hard problem" the brief anticipated. There is no constraint solver, no consistency checker, no propagation engine, no importance sampler, no estimator, no bias. There is a **set of realities**, and every game action is a **filter over that set**. The counter is not estimated — it is `aliveN`, an integer. The ghost fleets are not approximated — they are `alive[rng.int(0, aliveN-1)]`, exactly uniform. The defender is not heuristically evasive — it is provably, exactly, maximally evasive under the greedy criterion.

This is also *exactly* the nostromo-gambit doctrine ("честный отказ лучше подделанного десанта") transposed to the counter: we don't show an estimate dressed as a number.

### Measured universe sizes (all my own runs, exact enumeration or validated SIS)

| board | fleet | no-touch | count | how |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8×8 | [4,3,3,2] | yes | **3 562 232** | exact, 68 ms |
| 8×8 | [4,3,3,2] | no | 19 999 324 | exact, 396 ms |
| 8×8 | [4,3,3,2,2] | yes | 45 317 068 | exact, 1.5 s |
| 8×8 | [4,3,3,2,2] | no | 783 249 968 | exact, 16.8 s |
| 10×10 | [4,3,3,2] | yes | 7.26×10⁷ | SIS ±0.17% |
| 10×10 | [5,4,3,3,2] | yes | 1.92×10⁹ | SIS ±0.21% |
| 10×10 | [4,3,3,2,2,2,1,1,1,1] (Russian) | yes | **1.869×10¹⁵** | SIS ±2.1% |
| 10×10 | Russian | no | 1.328×10¹⁸ | SIS ±1.0% |

Placement counts: 8×8 → L4:80, L3:96, L2:112, L1:64. 10×10 → L4:140, L3:160, L2:180, L1:100. All < 256, so a placement index is one byte — that's what makes the 4-byte config encoding work.

### RECOMMENDATION: canonical mode is 8×8, fleet [4,3,3,2], no-touch

Not because it's easy, but because it is the largest configuration where the game can be **exactly truthful** for its entire duration, and 3.5 million is a perfect headline number: big enough to feel like a multiverse, small enough that the counter reaches 1 in front of you.

Offer 10×10 Russian as a second mode («БЕЗДНА», 1.87 квадриллиона реальностей) built on Tier 1 below — but ship 8×8 as the default and the tuned experience.

## Tier 0 — the materialised multiverse (canonical mode)

**Representation.** One `Uint8Array(4 × C)`. Config *i* = bytes `[i*4 .. i*4+3]` = placement indices of ship-4, ship-3a, ship-3b, ship-2. Identical ships stored in canonical increasing index order (`3a < 3b`), so the array enumerates *sets*, not sequences — no `/k!` correction anywhere. Cache-friendly, sequential, no pointer chasing, no index array.

**Constraint set = the array itself.** After answer *a* at turn *t*, we compact the array in place, keeping only configs that would have given *a*. Write cursor ≤ read cursor always, so memory never grows and never reallocates. The critical consequence: **the time-indexed "hit but not sunk" constraint needs no bookkeeping at all.** It is enforced automatically because we filtered by the answer computed against the shot-set *as it stood at that moment*. Every constraint the brief worried about — misses empty, hits occupied, killed ship fully within the then-current shots, dead-ship halo empty, each live-hit ship having a surviving unshot cell — is a consequence of having filtered correctly at the time. There is nothing to get wrong later.

**Per-turn work.** Three passes at most:
1. `buildTurnTables(cell)` — 288 bytes of lookup (T4[80], T3[96], T2[112]), values `0` = placement doesn't cover the cell, `1` = covers it and survives the shot, `2` = covers it and dies. Costs 288 iterations. This turns the inner loop from bit arithmetic into **pure array lookups**.
2. `partition` — one linear pass, ≤4 byte loads + ≤4 table lookups per config, incrementing `Int32Array(290)` bucket counters (key 0 = MISS, 1 = HIT, 2+pid = KILL of that specific placement).
3. `compact` — one linear pass keeping the chosen bucket.

The histogram pass (for ghosts + the player's density HUD) is a fourth pass that increments 4 per-placement counters, then expands 288 placement counts into 64 cell counts. Expansion is O(288), not O(C) — a 3× saving over counting cells directly.

## Tier 1 — sampling (10×10 / bigger fleets)

Exact enumeration on 10×10 Russian is hopeless *for almost the whole game*, and I measured exactly how hopeless: with a 40-million-node budget, a constrained DFS could not complete **until shot 78**, and only got fast (<150 ms) at **shot 84**. So a 10×10 mode is a sampling mode for 80% of its length. Design accordingly and label it honestly in the UI.

Tier 1 = a population of K uniform particles maintained by **Gibbs resampling** (pick a ship, enumerate all its legal placements given the others + the history, choose uniformly — this is exact Gibbs, uniform-stationary), seeded by **SIS restarts**, with the counter driven by a **log-space ratio estimator** anchored on a baked-in constant. Details in `counting`.

Rejected alternatives and why: *rejection sampling* — dies at ~10 constraints, unusable; *DLX/exact cover* — ships aren't an exact cover (empty water is legal), and adapting it buys nothing over the byte-array scan; *DP over columns with a broken profile* — for no-touch battleship the profile state is {empty, terminated, pending-1..3}^10 × 120 fleet-count states ≈ 10⁹, worse than sampling and vastly more code; *per-ship mask intersection with propagation* — gives feasibility, not counts, and counts are the product.

## Three findings that change the game design

**1. The two clocks problem — the multiverse collapses long before the fleet sinks.** Against an optimal player, `N` reaches **1 at shot 31**, but the last ship isn't physically sunk until **shot 62**. Half the game is a mop-up where the player already knows everything. → **Victory condition must be `N == 1`, not "all ships sunk".** Thematically this is the *better* game: you don't sink the fleet, you pin reality until it has nowhere left to be. Then the final cinematic salvo auto-destroys the now-determined fleet. Par ≈ 31, information-theoretic floor = log₂(3 562 232) = **21.76 bits** ⇒ 22 shots. That is a tight, scoreable, replayable 25–35 shot game with a visible perfect score.

**2. The determinism trap.** With a deterministic max-mass defender and no hidden state, *there is no hidden state* — the optimal line is identical every single game. My "split" player scored 31, 31, 31, 31, 31, 31, 31, 31 across eight seeds. Two fixes, both needed: **(a) rift cells** — 2–4 seeded cells no ship may occupy, added to the forbidden mask at build time; the universe is different (and differently sized) every game, so the counter opens on a fresh number like «3 214 118 РЕАЛЬНОСТЕЙ»; **(b) ε-slack answer selection** — among buckets within a factor (1−ε) of the largest, choose by seeded weighted RNG. ε is the difficulty knob and is a direct transposition of nostromo's `slackCp` doctrine (weaken by choosing among near-optimal answers, never by crippling the search).

**3. The all-misses problem.** Under max-mass greedy the defender says MISS almost always — on turn 1 the *densest* cell on the board is occupied in only 22.2% of realities, so the best a shot can do is a 78/22 split = **0.36 bits**. The optimal 31-shot line contains 25 misses, 6 hits and **zero kills before the pin.** A conventional battleship framing would be emotionally flat. → Reframe the feedback: a "miss" is not a miss, it is a **measurement that annihilates 22–43% of all realities**, and the counter + writhing ghost fleet is the payoff. Measured drop-per-shot along the optimal line: −22%, −23%, −26%, −26%, −30%, −30%, −32%, −33%, −36%, −37%, −39%, −43%… an accelerating, always-satisfying curve. Then give the player the **БРАНА-ТОРПЕДА**, which forces the *minimum*-mass answer (guaranteed hit if any reality holds a ship there) as the rare, expensive, spectacular button.

**4. The HUD is the mechanic, not decoration.** A parity hunt/target player (no HUD reasoning) needs **48.3 turns** to pin reality; a density-guided player needs **31**. The ghost fleet and the counter are what make the game the right length. Without them the evasive defender costs a naive player only ~5 shots over a static one — the twist would be invisible. This is the strongest possible argument for the ghost-fleet HUD being load-bearing.

```js
// oracle/universe.js — исполняется в воркере, наружу не выходит ни байта массива.
const N = 8;

function placements(L) {                       // все размещения корабля длины L
  const list = [];
  for (let r = 0; r < N; r++) for (let c = 0; c < N; c++) {
    const dirs = L === 1 ? [[0, 1]] : [[0, 1], [1, 0]];
    for (const [dr, dc] of dirs) {
      const cells = []; let ok = true;
      for (let i = 0; i < L; i++) {
        const rr = r + dr * i, cc = c + dc * i;
        if (rr >= N || cc >= N) { ok = false; break; }
        cells.push(rr * N + cc);
      }
      if (ok) list.push(cells);
    }
  }
  return list;
}

// 64 клетки = два слова по 32 бита. o — корпус, h — корпус вместе с ореолом
// (правило «корабли не касаются» проверяется как o одного ∩ h другого).
function mask(cells) {
  let o0 = 0, o1 = 0, h0 = 0, h1 = 0;
  const put = (b, halo) => { if (b < 32) { halo ? h0 |= 1 << b : o0 |= 1 << b; }
                             else       { halo ? h1 |= 1 << (b - 32) : o1 |= 1 << (b - 32); } };
  for (const c of cells) {
    put(c, 0);
    const r = (c / N) | 0, cc = c % N;
    for (let dr = -1; dr <= 1; dr++) for (let dc = -1; dc <= 1; dc++) {
      const rr = r + dr, c2 = cc + dc;
      if (rr < 0 || rr >= N || c2 < 0 || c2 >= N) continue;
      put(rr * N + c2, 1);
    }
  }
  return { o0, o1, h0, h1, cells };
}

const L4 = placements(4).map(mask), L3 = placements(3).map(mask), L2 = placements(2).map(mask);
const SLOT = [L4, L3, L3, L2];        // 4 слота флота [4,3,3,2]
const PBASE = [0, 80, 80, 176];       // смещения глобальных id размещений (всего 288)

// Разломы: seeded клетки, куда корабль встать не может. Это единственный источник
// различий между партиями — без них оптимальная линия одна и та же навсегда.
function riftMask(rng, count) {
  let r0 = 0, r1 = 0;
  const taken = new Set();
  while (taken.size < count) {
    const c = rng.int(0, 63);
    if (taken.has(c)) continue;
    taken.add(c);
    if (c < 32) r0 |= 1 << c; else r1 |= 1 << (c - 32);
  }
  return { r0, r1, cells: [...taken] };
}

function buildUniverse(rift) {
  // Ёмкость с запасом; реальный размер вернём отдельно. 3 562 232 при 0 разломов.
  const CAP = 3_600_000;
  const ships = new Uint8Array(CAP * 4);
  let n = 0;
  for (let a = 0; a < L4.length; a++) {
    const A = L4[a];
    if (A.o0 & rift.r0 || A.o1 & rift.r1) continue;
    for (let b = 0; b < L3.length; b++) {
      const B = L3[b];
      if (B.o0 & rift.r0 || B.o1 & rift.r1) continue;
      if (B.o0 & A.h0 || B.o1 & A.h1) continue;
      const g0 = A.h0 | B.h0, g1 = A.h1 | B.h1;
      for (let c = b + 1; c < L3.length; c++) {         // c > b — канонический порядок
        const C = L3[c];                                 // считаем МНОЖЕСТВА, не наборы
        if (C.o0 & rift.r0 || C.o1 & rift.r1) continue;
        if (C.o0 & g0 || C.o1 & g1) continue;
        const q0 = g0 | C.h0, q1 = g1 | C.h1;
        for (let d = 0; d < L2.length; d++) {
          const D = L2[d];
          if (D.o0 & rift.r0 || D.o1 & rift.r1) continue;
          if (D.o0 & q0 || D.o1 & q1) continue;
          const z = n * 4;
          ships[z] = a; ships[z + 1] = b; ships[z + 2] = c; ships[z + 3] = d;
          n++;
        }
      }
    }
  }
  return { ships, aliveN: n, total: n };
}
```

## 2. The one primitive: partition → choose → compact

Every weapon in the game is this function with a different `keyOf` and a different `policy`. Shot, salvo, count-probe, Geller field, brane torpedo — one code path.

```js
const KEY_MISS = 0, KEY_HIT = 1, KEY_KILL = 2;   // KEY_KILL + globalPlacementId

// Таблицы хода: 288 байт. После них внутренний цикл — только чтение массивов,
// ни одной битовой операции на конфигурацию. Это даёт ~3× против битовых тестов.
function buildShotTables(cell, nshot0, nshot1) {
  const w = cell < 32 ? 0 : 1;
  const bit = cell < 32 ? (1 << cell) : (1 << (cell - 32));
  const fill = (list, T) => {
    for (let i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      const p = list[i];
      if (!((w === 0 ? p.o0 : p.o1) & bit)) { T[i] = 0; continue; }   // не накрывает
      // 2 — корабль целиком внутри уже отстрелянных клеток ⇒ этот выстрел его убивает
      T[i] = ((p.o0 & ~nshot0) === 0 && (p.o1 & ~nshot1) === 0) ? 2 : 1;
    }
  };
  fill(L4, T4); fill(L3, T3); fill(L2, T2);
}

// Ключ ответа для одной конфигурации. Ровно один слот может накрывать клетку —
// корабли не пересекаются, поэтому первое совпадение и есть ответ.
function keyOfShot(ships, z) {
  let v;
  if ((v = T4[ships[z    ]])) return v === 1 ? KEY_HIT : KEY_KILL + PBASE[0] + ships[z];
  if ((v = T3[ships[z + 1]])) return v === 1 ? KEY_HIT : KEY_KILL + PBASE[1] + ships[z + 1];
  if ((v = T3[ships[z + 2]])) return v === 1 ? KEY_HIT : KEY_KILL + PBASE[2] + ships[z + 2];
  if ((v = T2[ships[z + 3]])) return v === 1 ? KEY_HIT : KEY_KILL + PBASE[3] + ships[z + 3];
  return KEY_MISS;
}

function partition(U, keyOf, nKeys) {
  const cnt = new Int32Array(nKeys);              // Int32Array, НЕ Map: детерминированный
  for (let i = 0, z = 0; i < U.aliveN; i++, z += 4) cnt[keyOf(U.ships, z)]++;   // порядок обхода
  return cnt;
}

// Единственное место, где вообще есть случайность в решениях защитника.
function chooseBucket(cnt, policy, eps, rng) {
  let best = 0;
  for (let k = 0; k < cnt.length; k++) if (cnt[k] > cnt[best]) best = k;
  if (policy === 'torpedo') {                     // брана-торпеда: минимальная масса
    let mn = -1;                                  // из НЕПУСТЫХ — максимально невыгодный
    for (let k = 0; k < cnt.length; k++)          // для бога ответ. Он всё ещё не лжёт.
      if (cnt[k] > 0 && (mn < 0 || cnt[k] < cnt[mn])) mn = k;
    return mn;
  }
  if (eps <= 0) return best;                      // 5 уровень: чистая жадность
  const floor = cnt[best] * (1 - eps);            // «люфт»: всё, что почти так же хорошо
  const pool = [];
  for (let k = 0; k < cnt.length; k++) if (cnt[k] >= floor && cnt[k] > 0) pool.push(k);
  // pool уже отсортирован по возрастанию k — детерминированно при том же сиде.
  return rng.weighted(pool, (k) => cnt[k]);
}

function compact(U, keyOf, chosen) {
  let w = 0;
  for (let i = 0, z = 0; i < U.aliveN; i++, z += 4) {
    if (keyOf(U.ships, z) !== chosen) continue;
    const a = U.ships[z], b = U.ships[z+1], c = U.ships[z+2], d = U.ships[z+3];
    const y = w * 4;                              // читаем в локальные ДО записи:
    U.ships[y] = a; U.ships[y+1] = b;             // w ≤ i, но при w === i это
    U.ships[y+2] = c; U.ships[y+3] = d;           // самоперезапись через алиас.
    w++;
  }
  U.aliveN = w;
}
```

```js
function answerShot(U, S, cell, opts) {
  const w = cell < 32 ? 0 : 1, bit = cell < 32 ? (1 << cell) : (1 << (cell - 32));
  const n0 = S.shot0 | (w === 0 ? bit : 0), n1 = S.shot1 | (w === 1 ? bit : 0);
  buildShotTables(cell, n0, n1);

  const keyOf = keyOfShot;
  const cnt = partition(U, keyOf, 2 + 288);
  const chosen = chooseBucket(cnt, opts.policy, opts.eps, S.rngDefender);

  const before = U.aliveN;
  compact(U, keyOf, chosen);
  S.shot0 = n0; S.shot1 = n1;

  // Инвариант, ради которого всё и построено. Если он когда-нибудь падает — это
  // не «не нашлось расстановки», это ошибка в коде фильтра.
  if (U.aliveN === 0) throw new Error('[оракул] множество реальностей опустело');

  return {
    answer: chosen === KEY_MISS ? 'MISS' : chosen === KEY_HIT ? 'HIT' : 'KILL',
    killedShip: chosen >= KEY_KILL ? placementCells(chosen - KEY_KILL) : null,
    before, after: U.aliveN,
    collapsed: before - U.aliveN,                 // сколько реальностей мы стёрли
    bits: Math.log2(before / U.aliveN),           // «−0.42 БИТА» в журнал
  };
}
```

```js
function marginals(U) {
  const m4 = new Int32Array(80), m3 = new Int32Array(96), m2 = new Int32Array(112);

  for (let i = 0; i < 112; i++) if (m2[i]) for (const c of L2[i].cells) cell[c] += m2[i];
  return { m4, m3, m2, cell };                    // cell[c] / aliveN = плотность призраков

  const out = [];
```

```js
// по возрастанию индекса) означает, что оценивается число МНОЖЕСТВ напрямую,
// без деления на произведение факториалов.
function sisSample(P, order, forbidMask, liveHits, rng) {
  const occ = new Int32Array(W), halo = new Int32Array(W);
  let w = 1, prevLen = -1, prevIdx = -1;
  const cand = new Int32Array(400);
  for (const L of order) {
    const list = P[L];
    const start = (L === prevLen) ? prevIdx + 1 : 0;
    let nc = 0;
    for (let i = start; i < list.length; i++) {
      const p = list[i];
      if (conflicts(p, halo, W)) continue;
      if (intersects(p.o, forbidMask, W)) continue;
      // Отсечение: корабль, накрывший «раненую» клетку, обязан иметь
      // хотя бы одну неотстрелянную — иначе он был бы уже убит.
      if (intersects(p.o, liveHits, W) && subsetOf(p.o, shotMask, W)) continue;
      cand[nc++] = i;
    }
    if (nc === 0) return { ok: false, w: 0 };     // тупик — вес 0, НО образец учитывается
    w *= nc;                                      // в знаменателе: иначе оценка смещена
    const pick = cand[rng.int(0, nc - 1)];
    apply(list[pick], occ, halo, W);
    prevLen = L; prevIdx = pick;
  }
  if (!coversAll(occ, liveHits, W)) return { ok: false, w: 0 };
  return { ok: true, w, occ };
}

function sisCount(P, order, constraints, K, rng) {
  let sum = 0, sum2 = 0;
  for (let k = 0; k < K; k++) { const s = sisSample(P, order, ...constraints, rng); sum += s.w; sum2 += s.w * s.w; }
  const mean = sum / K, se = Math.sqrt((sum2 / K - mean * mean) / K);
  return { est: mean, rse: se / mean };           // проверено: 8×8 [4,3,3,2] → 3.5635e6
}                                                 // против точных 3 562 232, ошибка 0.04%

// Гиббс: убираем один корабль, перечисляем ВСЕ его законные размещения при
// остальных зафиксированных, выбираем равномерно. Стационарное распределение —
// точно равномерное на множестве согласованных расстановок. Текущее размещение
// всегда входит в список кандидатов, поэтому цепь не может застрять.
function gibbsSweep(cfg, P, constraints, rng) {
  for (let s = 0; s < cfg.ships.length; s++) {
    const others = occupancyWithout(cfg, s);
    const uncovered = andNot(constraints.liveHits, others.occ);
    const list = P[cfg.ships[s].len];
    const cand = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      const p = list[i];
      if (intersects(p.o, others.halo, W)) continue;
      if (intersects(p.o, constraints.forbid, W)) continue;
      if (!supersetOf(p.o, uncovered, W)) continue;             // обязан накрыть сирот
      if (intersects(p.o, constraints.liveHits, W) && subsetOf(p.o, constraints.shots, W)) continue;
      cand.push(i);
    }
    cfg.ships[s].idx = cand[rng.int(0, cand.length - 1)];       // cand непуст всегда:
  }                                                             // текущее размещение в нём
}
```

Counting the realities: ## Tier 0: the count is not estimated. It is `aliveN`.

`aliveN` is an `Int32` in the range [1, 3 562 232]. It is the exact number of complete legal fleet placements consistent with the entire answer history. No estimator, no confidence interval, no jitter, no bias, no floating point. The UI prints it with no «≈» and the game may say so out loud, in the house voice:

> «СЧЁТЧИК НЕ ОЦЕНИВАЕТ. ОН ПЕРЕСЧИТЫВАЕТ. КАЖДУЮ.»

Monotonicity is structural, not enforced: `alive_{t+1} ⊆ alive_t` because compaction is a filter over the same array. The counter mathematically cannot go up, cannot jitter, and cannot disagree with the ghost fleet (both read the same array).

Two derived numbers worth showing, both exact and both free:
- **Collapse per shot**: `before − after`, e.g. «СТЁРТО 789 988 РЕАЛЬНОСТЕЙ».
- **Bits**: `log2(before / after)`. The header can carry «ОСТАЛОСЬ 21.76 БИТ» ticking down to 0. This makes the information-theoretic floor (22 shots) legible as a *par*, and it is the single best explanation of why some shots are wasted: a shot at a cell where every reality agrees yields exactly 0.00 bits and the counter does not move.

Rendering rule: below 10 000 print the exact integer with thin-space grouping («8 074»); above that, either the full grouped integer or 3 significant digits + power («3.56 × 10⁶») — but never switch representation mid-fall in a way that looks like a jump. I'd print the full grouped integer always; watching «3 562 232» → «2 772 244» digit-by-digit is the drama.

## Tier 1 (10×10): honest estimation, three layers

**Layer A — the anchor N₀ is a compile-time constant.** For a fixed board+fleet the starting count is a number, not a computation. Bake it in with a comment recording how it was obtained:

```js
// Русский флот 10×10, корабли не касаются. Посчитано SIS-оценкой на 2·10⁶ образцов,
// относительная ошибка 0.7%. Точного перечисления не существует: DFS с бюджетом
// 4·10⁷ узлов не завершается до 78-го выстрела.
const N0 = 1.869e15;
```
(My measured values: Russian no-touch **1.8692×10¹⁵ ±2.12%** at K=200k; touching **1.3283×10¹⁸ ±0.99%**. Ship the number computed at K=2×10⁶ offline for ±0.7%.)

**Layer B — the running counter is a log-space ratio product.** Never estimate the absolute count mid-game; estimate only the *survival fraction* of the chosen answer, which is a ratio of counts from one population and is far lower-variance than an absolute count:

```js
// log-пространство: произведение сорока дробей в обычных числах уползает,
// а сумма логарифмов — нет. И 1.87e15 < 2^53, но 1.33e18 уже нет.
S.logN = Math.log(N0);
// каждый ход:
const f = cnt[chosen] / K;                    // доля популяции, пережившая ответ
S.logN += Math.log(f);
const shown = Math.exp(S.logN);
```
Because the population is uniform (maintained by Gibbs, not by weights), `cnt[chosen]/K` is an unbiased estimator of the true survival fraction, and the ratio form means the K in numerator and denominator largely cancels.

**Layer C — monotone clamp + honest labelling.** `display = min(display_prev, shown)`, floored at 1, printed with a leading «≈». The clamp is justified: the true count is provably non-increasing, so clamping only ever moves the estimate *toward* a value we know is an upper bound. It is a conservative, monotone, non-lying presentation — and the «≈» says exactly what it is.

**Layer D — exact takeover.** Every turn, run the constrained DFS counter with a node budget (I used 4×10⁷; a browser budget of 2×10⁶ nodes ≈ 50 ms is right). If it completes, **drop the «≈» and print the exact integer for the rest of the game.** Measured takeover point on 10×10 Russian with random firing: shot 78 (323 ms at 3.5M nodes), comfortable by shot 84 (51 ms), trivial by shot 90 (1 ms). So the last ~15 shots — the climax — are exactly counted. The moment the «≈» disappears is itself a dramatic beat: «ОЦЕНКА → ПЕРЕСЧЁТ».

**The SIS estimator, named and specified.** Sequential importance sampling with canonical ordering, uniform proposal over the surviving candidate set at each step:

  N̂ = (1/K) Σₖ wₖ,  wₖ = Π_{j=1..m} |C_j^{(k)}|  (wₖ = 0 for dead-end draws, which are *counted in K*)

where `C_j` is the set of legal placements of ship *j* given ships 1..j−1 and the constraint set, and identical ships are restricted to increasing placement index so the sample space is in bijection with *sets* of placements — no `Π kᵢ!` correction. This is Knuth's estimator generalised (Chen–Diaconis–Holmes–Liu sequential Monte Carlo for counting). Variance estimate: `SE = sqrt((Σw² /K − N̂²)/K)`.

**Validation is not optional and I ran it:** on 8×8 [4,3,3,2] where the truth is exactly 3 562 232, SIS gave **3 563 541** at K=200 000 (error **+0.04%**, quoted RSE 0.21% — well inside one sigma) in 965 ms, and 3 554 400 at K=20 000 (error −0.22%, RSE 0.68%) in 130 ms. Dead-end fraction 9.0%. That comparison must exist as a unit test in the shipped project: *the estimator is checked against a number the game can compute exactly*. That is precisely the nostromo-gambit oracle doctrine (self-play with invariants on every ply) applied to a counter.

Dead-end fractions rise with fleet density — 3.6% for 10×10 [4,3,3,2], 5.4% for [5,4,3,3,2], **68.6%** for the Russian fleet. High dead-end fraction is the warning light for variance; if it exceeds ~85%, add look-ahead pruning (reject a candidate if any *later* ship provably has no placement) before increasing K, since pruning cuts variance while K only cuts it as 1/√K.

**Effective sample size.** Track `ESS = (Σw)² / Σw²`. If ESS < 200, the displayed number is not trustworthy at 3 significant digits — round harder (2 sig figs) rather than showing precision you don't have. Widening the displayed precision instead of faking it is the same move as nostromo's «ДОПУСК РАСШИРЕН ДО ±45 СП» written into the log.

1. *Per-turn lookup tables (288 bytes) instead of bit tests in the inner loop.* The inner loop becomes 4 byte loads + ≤4 byte lookups, no shifts, no masks.
2. *Marginals over placements, not cells.* 4 increments per config instead of 12, then O(288) expansion. ~3× on the histogram pass.
3. *In-place compaction, no index array.* Sequential access instead of a gathered read through `alive[i]`, and it saves 14 MB. 4. *Fuse partition and compaction* when the answer policy is pure greedy on a cheap key — or accept two passes (I measured two passes; it's already fast enough, and two passes is clearer code).

Correctness / never-lies: ## The defender provably never lies

**Invariant I.** At the start of every turn, `alive` is exactly the set of complete legal fleet placements consistent with the full answer history, and `|alive| ≥ 1`.

**Base case.** `alive₀` = all placements enumerated by `buildUniverse` — legal by construction (no overlap, no touching, no rift cell), consistent with an empty history, and non-empty (3 562 232 > 0; with rifts, assert `> 0` at build time and re-roll the rift seed if a pathological rift set empties it — cannot happen with ≤4 rift cells, but assert anyway).

**Inductive step.** On a shot at cell *c*, `keyOfShot` is a **total function** on `alive`: every configuration maps to exactly one key, because ships never overlap so at most one slot covers *c*, and the kill test `(p.o & ~nshot) === 0` is a decidable predicate on that slot. Therefore the keys **partition** `alive`:  `alive = ⊎_k bucket_k`, and `Σ_k cnt[k] = |alive|`.

`chooseBucket` returns a key with `cnt[chosen] ≥ 1` — for the greedy policy because the argmax of a partition of a non-empty set is non-empty; for the ε-slack policy because the pool is filtered on `cnt[k] > 0`; for the torpedo policy because the min is taken over non-empty buckets only. Hence `alive' = bucket_chosen ≠ ∅`.

Every member of `bucket_chosen` is, by the definition of the key function, a configuration that *would have produced exactly the answer we gave*, and it was already consistent with all prior answers by the inductive hypothesis. So `alive'` is exactly the consistent set for the extended history, and it is non-empty. ∎

**The answer is therefore always backed by an explicit witness**, and not just one: `cnt[chosen]` of them, each materially present in memory as four bytes. At any moment the game can be asked "prove it" and hand back a concrete fleet — a real feature worth shipping («ПОКАЗАТЬ ОДНУ ИЗ РЕАЛЬНОСТЕЙ», draws a sampled config solid).

**The subtle constraint that is handled for free.** The literature-hard part of this problem is the *time-indexed* nature of a hit: "hit, not sunk" at turn *t* asserts that the ship covering *c* had an unshot cell **as of turn t**, and a later shot may legitimately sink it. Any implementation that maintains an explicit constraint set has to carry the shot-set snapshot per answer and re-check it. Here it evaporates: we filtered at turn *t* using `nshot_t`, and the survivors are permanently those that satisfied it. There is no constraint object to get wrong. **This is the single strongest argument for population-as-constraint over solver-as-constraint, and it should be the load-bearing comment at the top of the oracle file.**

**Tier 1 (sampling) needs one extra guarantee**, because there the population is a *sample* of the consistent set, not the set. Maintain `W` — a single witness configuration, always consistent with the full history:
- Each turn, after choosing an answer, set `W := ` any particle in the chosen bucket (there is at least one, or we would not have chosen it).
- If the population is empty or every bucket is empty (sampler failure, not a logical impossibility), **answer as `W` would answer**. `W` is consistent with the whole history by induction, so its answer is legal. The defender degrades from "maximally evasive" to "honest but dumb" — never to "liar".
- Log it: «ОРАКУЛ ОСЛЕП — ОТВЕТ ПО ЯКОРНОЙ ВЕТКЕ». Visible honest degradation, exactly like «ДОПУСК РАСШИРЕН ДО ±45 СП».

## Termination and winnability

**Termination.** Every shot targets a previously unshot cell (the UI must forbid re-shooting, and should, since it yields 0 bits anyway). The potential function `unshotCells` strictly decreases, so the game ends within 64 turns (100 on 10×10). At `unshotCells = 0` every cell's occupancy is determined by the answers, so `|alive| = 1` and every ship is fully within the shot set — meaning every ship was answered KILL at some point. **The player always wins; the only question is in how many shots.** There is no losing state and no draw.

**Under the recommended victory rule (`N == 1`) it terminates much sooner**, and I measured it rather than assuming: 31 turns against an optimal density-guided player (8/8 seeds), 44–52 turns against a parity hunt/target player (mean 48.3), 26–30 with two region probes spent. Information-theoretic floor log₂(3 562 232) = **21.76 bits**, and since a shot has ≥2 outcomes it yields ≤1 bit, so **22 shots is the absolute minimum** and 31 is the realistic par. That gives a clean scoring band: ≤26 «ПРОРОК», 27–31 «НАВИГАТОР», 32–40 «СЛЕПЕЦ».

**Non-degeneracy.** There is no "no valid configuration" state to guard against, because we never construct constraints — we only remove elements from a non-empty set. If `aliveN` ever hits 0, that is not a game state, it is a bug in `compact` or a mismatch between the partition key function and the compaction key function (they must be literally the same function; do not write it twice). `throw new Error('[оракул] множество реальностей опустело')` and let it be loud.

**One more property worth asserting in tests.** The counter must be *consistent with the ghosts*: `density[c] === 0` ⟺ no sampled ghost occupies `c`, and `density[c] === aliveN` ⟺ every ghost occupies it. Cheap invariant, catches key/compaction desync immediately. Alongside: a self-play harness that plays N games with random player policies and asserts on every turn that (a) `aliveN` strictly decreases or stays equal, (b) `aliveN ≥ 1`, (c) a brute-force re-derivation of the consistent set from the raw answer history equals the maintained `alive` set — checkable exactly at 8×8, which is the whole point of choosing 8×8. That is the direct analogue of nostromo's `npm run selfplay` oracle.
Salvos and region probes: ## Everything is one primitive: `partition(keyOf) → chooseBucket(policy) → compact()`

The four weapons differ only in **what the key is** and **which bucket the policy picks**. That is the whole weapon system, and it means new munitions cost ~15 lines each. Worth designing the code around explicitly.

| weapon | key function | policy | cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| ОБЫЧНЫЙ ВЫСТРЕЛ | miss / hit / kill(placementId) | max mass | 1 pass |
| ЗАЛП (m клеток) | tuple of m per-cell answers | max mass | 1 pass |
| ЗОНД (счётная волна) | `popcount(occ ∩ R)` | max mass | 1 pass |
| ПОЛЕ ГЕЛЛЕРА | full occupancy pattern `occ ∩ R` | max mass | 1 pass |
| БРАНА-ТОРПЕДА | miss / hit / kill | **min non-empty** | 1 pass |

### Salvo (simultaneous multi-cell shot)

The answer is a **tuple**, one entry per fired cell, and the population is partitioned by the whole tuple — not cell by cell. Partitioning cell-by-cell and then intersecting would be wrong: it could select a combination of individually-max answers that jointly has zero witnesses, i.e. a lie.

Implementation: build one shot-table triple per fired cell (all against the *post-salvo* shot mask `nshot`, because the salvo lands at once), then one pass over `alive` computing an m-entry signature, densifying signatures into small integer keys via a `Map` filled in traversal order (deterministic). Then the usual argmax + compact. Cost is one pass, m× the per-config work — a 3-cell salvo on turn 1 costs ~150 ms, which is why salvos should be a mid-game munition or the game should simply accept 150 ms in the worker.

**Kill attribution inside a salvo** needs a stated canonical rule, or the same salvo has two legal readings: if two cells of the same salvo complete one ship, the KILL is attributed to the **last cell in raster order** (`r*8+c` ascending) and the earlier one reports HIT. Sort the fired cells before building tables. Write the rule in the log so the player can verify it: «ЗАЛП D4·D5·D6 → МИМО · ПОПАДАНИЕ · УБИТ (3)».

**Why the joint form matters to the player**: a salvo is strictly more informative per shot than the same cells fired sequentially *for the player*, because the defender cannot adapt between them — but it is also strictly *worse*, because the defender picks the best joint answer with full knowledge of all m cells. These two effects are real and opposite; the joint partition is what makes the tradeoff honest. Do not pretend a salvo is just m shots.

### Count probe (счётная волна)

"How many ship cells lie inside region R?" Key = `popcount(occ ∩ R)`, values 0..12. Up to 13 buckets, so the theoretical yield is up to log₂13 = 3.7 bits, but the adversary takes the modal bucket so the practical yield is ~1–1.5 bits — **comparable to a single shot**. I measured this: two 3×3 count probes reduce the optimal game from 31.0 to 28.5 turns, i.e. **≈1.25 turns saved per probe**. So a probe that costs a turn is roughly break-even and therefore boring. Tune it by making the region larger (a full row/column/quadrant), or by making the probe cost a resource rather than a turn.

Note the fleet has 12 cells total, so a probe over the *whole board* always answers 12 and yields 0 bits — a nice teaching moment the UI should refuse politely rather than waste: «ВОЛНА СЛИШКОМ ШИРОКА — ОТВЕТ ИЗВЕСТЕН ЗАРАНЕЕ».

### Geller field (пузырь стабильной реальности) — the strong weapon

This is not a question, it is a **forced commitment**. Key = the full occupancy bit-pattern of `occ ∩ R` (for a 3×3 region, at most 2⁹ = 512 distinct patterns, and in practice far fewer because of the no-touch rule and the fleet's size). The defender must choose one pattern and live with it forever; every cell of R becomes determined in every surviving reality.

This is dramatically stronger than a count probe because it removes *all* internal degrees of freedom in R at once, not just one aggregate number. A 3×3 field typically collapses the counter by an order of magnitude in a single action — it is the cliff-edge moment the counter exists to dramatise, and it is literally «пришпилить реальность» from the seed brainstorm. Balance it as a once-or-twice-per-game resource.

Two follow-on consequences the UI gets for free: pinned cells are permanently painted (all realities agree), and shooting into a pinned region afterwards yields exactly 0.00 bits — which teaches, without a tutorial, that shots must be aimed where the multiverse is *undecided*. That is the whole skill of the game in one visual.

### Brane torpedo (брана-торпеда) — the fun button

Same key function as a normal shot, but `policy = 'torpedo'`: pick the **smallest non-empty** bucket. The god is forced into the answer it least wants, and since HIT/KILL buckets are almost always the minority (the densest cell on turn 1 is occupied in only 22.2% of realities), a torpedo is effectively a **guaranteed hit wherever a hit is possible at all**, plus the largest possible single-shot collapse of the counter. It is still 100% honest — the chosen bucket is non-empty, so a witness exists.

This is the answer to the emotional flatness of a max-mass defender that says MISS 80% of the time. Give the player 2–3 torpedoes per game. In fiction it is exactly the friend's line: «есть особый снаряд которым я могу накрыть сразу несколько альтернативных веток».

### One implementation note that ties them together

`chooseBucket(cnt, policy, eps, rng)` is the *only* place in the entire oracle where a decision is made, and the only place that consumes randomness. Every weapon, every difficulty level, and every replay determinism property funnels through those four arguments. Keep it that way.
Pitfalls: ## 1. Population collapse to zero
**Tier 0: structurally impossible** — buckets partition a non-empty set and we always pick a non-empty bucket. If it happens, it is a code bug (partition key ≠ compaction key), so *use the same function object for both*, never two copies. Assert `aliveN >= 1` after every compaction and throw loudly.
**Tier 1: possible** (sampler fails to find particles in the true set). Mitigation is the anchor witness `W` described in `correctness`: the defender falls back to answering as one known-consistent configuration would. Also monitor ESS and force a fresh SIS restart when ESS < 200 or when the dead-end fraction of the last batch exceeds 0.9.

## 2. The deterministic-puzzle trap — the biggest design bug, and it is invisible until you measure
With a deterministic greedy defender and *no hidden state*, there is literally nothing hidden: both sides face the same public information set, so the optimal line is identical in every playthrough. My optimal player scored **31, 31, 31, 31, 31, 31, 31, 31** across eight different seeds. The game would have zero replay value and a solved-once-solved-forever optimal opening.
Two fixes, both required:
- **Rift cells** (`riftMask`): 2–4 seeded cells no ship may occupy, folded into the universe build. Different universe, different size, different optimal line every game — and the counter opens on a fresh number each time, which is better theatre than a constant.
- **ε-slack answer selection**: among buckets within `(1−ε)` of the max, choose by seeded weighted RNG. `ε` is the difficulty table, in the nostromo idiom of weakening by choosing among near-optimal moves rather than by crippling the search:
  `1 СЛЕПОЙ ε=0.40 / 2 ШЕПЧУЩИЙ ε=0.22 / 3 ЛОЦМАН ε=0.10 / 4 АРХИВАРИУС ε=0.03 / 5 ТОТ, КТО ЗА БРАНОЙ ε=0` — «Полная жадность. Он не ошибётся ни разу.»

## 3. Sampler bias making the counter lie
**Tier 0 has no sampler**, and this is worth saying in the README as the project's central technical claim. Ghost fleets are `alive[rng.int(0, aliveN-1)]` — exactly uniform over the consistent set, with no weights, no burn-in, no correlation. Density is a full exact count, not a sample.
**Tier 1**: (a) never mix particles produced by different proposals in one estimate — mixing SIS-weighted survivors with fresh Gibbs particles silently biases the ratio; regenerate wholesale or keep the populations separate by role (Gibbs population for decisions and ratios, SIS batches for anchoring only). (b) Gibbs is uniform-stationary but **irreducibility is not guaranteed** on tightly-packed boards — a single-ship move may not connect all configurations. Mitigate with occasional two-ship block moves and periodic independent SIS restarts, and never claim uniformity you haven't tested. (c) *Validate the estimator against a case you can compute exactly* — the 8×8 test (3 563 541 vs 3 562 232, +0.04%) must be a shipped unit test, because it is the only thing standing between "estimator" and "made-up number".

## 4. Floating point
Tier 0 counts are `Int32` up to 3.56M — no float anywhere; use `Int32Array` for buckets, not `Array`. The density array can be `Float64Array` but the values are integers; keep them integral and divide only at render time.
Tier 1: 1.87×10¹⁵ is under 2⁵³ so it is an exact integer in a `Number`, but 1.33×10¹⁸ (touching variant) is **not** — and more importantly a product of ~40 survival ratios drifts and can underflow. **Accumulate the counter in log space** (`logN += Math.log(f)`) and exponentiate only for display. Never compare floats for the monotone clamp; compare the logs.

## 5. RNG determinism and replay
- `Math.random` must appear **zero** times in the oracle. Use `makeRng(seed)` from `src/game/rng.mjs` unchanged, and `fork(label)` per subsystem: `rng.fork('rift')`, `rng.fork('defender')`, `rng.fork('ghosts')`. Without forks, adding one ghost draw shifts every defender decision and old replays break.
- **Map iteration order is a determinism hazard.** Anywhere a bucket set is built from a `Map` (salvos, Geller patterns), the argmax over a `Map` depends on insertion order, which depends on the traversal order of `alive`, which depends on prior compactions. It happens to be deterministic, but it is fragile. Prefer a dense `Int32Array` indexed by key; where a `Map` is unavoidable, **sort the keys before `chooseBucket`** so the RNG consumes draws in a stable order.
- A replay is `{ seed, riftCount, difficulty, shots: [...] }` — nothing else. That is enough to reconstruct the entire game bit-for-bit, which makes bug reports reproducible and makes a «ПОВТОРИТЬ ПАРТИЮ» feature free.

## 6. In-place compaction aliasing
`compact` writes to index `w*4` while reading from `i*4` with `w ≤ i`. When `w === i` the write is a self-overwrite through an alias. Read all four bytes into locals **before** the first store. I hit this while writing the benchmark; it produces a corrupted universe that still looks plausible for several turns — the worst kind of bug. Guard it with the ghost/density consistency assert.

## 7. The one-byte assumption
Placement indices fit in `Uint8Array` only because every list is < 256 (max 180, for length-2 on 10×10). Assert `list.length < 256` at build time and switch the whole array to `Uint16Array` if a future fleet breaks it. Silent truncation here would be catastrophic and invisible.

## 8. The two-clocks problem
Pin at turn 31, last ship sunk at turn 62. Shipping "sink all ships" as the victory condition means half the game is a known-answer mop-up. Victory must be `N == 1`. (Detailed in `approach`.)

## 9. Emotional flatness of a truthful adversary
25 misses / 6 hits / 0 kills along the optimal line. Handled by reframing miss→«РЕАЛЬНОСТЬ СМЕЩАЕТСЯ» with the counter as the payoff, plus the brane torpedo. But be aware it is a real risk: if the ghost fleet and counter are not *immediately* legible, the game reads as "I keep missing" and is abandoned in 90 seconds. The first three shots must teach the loop with no words: big number, big drop, ghosts visibly writhing and thinning.

## 10. Accessibility: flickering ghosts are a genuine hazard
"Faint flickering silhouettes" at high frequency is a photosensitivity risk, not just a taste question. Cap the ghost re-roll at ≤3 Hz, keep contrast low (`--phosphor-faint` on `--dark-square`), and under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` **stop the flicker entirely** and render a static density heat instead. The reference project has three `prefers-reduced-motion` guards; this project needs a fourth and it is the most important one in either codebase.

## 11. Memory pressure on the wrong platform
13.6 MB is fine; 226 MB (the [4,3,3,2,2] variant) is not. Do not let a "just add one more ship" settings option quietly cross the materialisation ceiling. Gate fleet selection so any fleet whose universe exceeds ~10M configs is explicitly marked as approximate mode in the UI, with the «≈» on the counter — and say so on the start screen the way nostromo says Fischer castling is off.

## 12. Worker availability
Blob-URL workers can be blocked by CSP in some embedding contexts. Detect at boot (`try { new Worker(url) } catch`), and fall back to the `requestAnimationFrame` time-sliced path rather than blocking the main thread for 103 ms. Print the mode in the boot sequence — «ОРАКУЛ · ОТДЕЛЬНЫЙ ПОТОК» vs «ОРАКУЛ · РАЗДЕЛЕНИЕ КАДРОВ» — because an honest status line is cheaper than a mystery stutter.
